subject: Integration pulse: SDK environment & local lab repro
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@lumina.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration pulse: SDK environment & local lab repro

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the sync today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the lab run: 

1) Goal: get a small local proof-of-concept that mirrors your expected production flow — SDK calls (Python + TypeScript), auth, routing to us-west, structured output/tool calling for a retrieval step, and an embeddings + reranker validation using a small test dataset.

2) Tech priorities we discussed (high level):
   - SDKs: Python (>=3.9) and TypeScript. We’ll share minimal sample apps that run locally (no cloud credentials required) and a Docker compose for the runtime.
   - Auth: two paths — API key for quick lab access, and SSO/OAuth for longer-term. For the lab we recommend API key scoped to a test project.
   - Routing: region pinning to us-west-2 with fallback to hosted model variants if dedicated capacity is exhausted. We’ll show how to configure routing policies in the SDK config file.
   - Structured output / tool calling: a small retrieval chain that calls a mock search tool. We'll demonstrate the function-calling payload and how Redwood returns tool output vs. model-generated text.
   - Embeddings & reranker: provide a small sample corpus (1k docs) and demonstrate embedding generation + a lightweight reranker (cosine + top-k). We’ll include an eval script to reproduce the ranking quality metric.

3) Lab artifacts we will provide (attached/links):
   - sdkenv-checklist.md (attached) — environment steps and local sanity checks
   - sample-app-python.zip — minimal Flask app that calls the Redwood SDK end-to-end (attached)
   - GitHub repo with TypeScript sample and docker-compose link (below)

4) Asks from your side:
   - Confirm whether we can provision a scoped API key for the Lumina test account (us-west-2).
   - Share a small representative sample (CSV or S3) for the 1k-doc corpus or confirm we should generate synthetic data.
   - Any network constraints (e.g., IP allowlist) for your internal CI runners.

Next steps: once you confirm API key access we’ll send a single compressed bundle with the samples and a one-page runbook. I’m proposing a 30-minute lab kickoff on Tue 5/25 to run through setup and smoke tests.

Thanks — I’ll attach the checklist and sample app in my next message.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Thanks for the recap — I added a few implementation notes below that’ll help Alex reproduce locally without cloud dependencies. Quoting Soojin’s note for context.

On Sat, 22 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700 Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> (recap omitted)

Karthik’s notes (actionable):
- Local runtime: we’ll provide a docker-compose.yml that spins up the sample app plus a mock search service (simple Flask app serving JSON). The sample-app-python.zip includes a compose file and a Makefile with targets: make build, make run, make smoke-test.
- SDK versions: pin to redwood-sdk==1.4.0 for Python and @redwood/sdk@1.4.0 for TS to ensure stable structured-output APIs.
- Auth scaffolding: include an environment file (.env.example) showing REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_REGION. For local development the SDK falls back to REDWOOD_API_KEY in env vars; production uses KMS-backed secrets.
- Routing config sample (redwood.yaml):
  routing: 
    primary_region: us-west-2
    fallback_regions: [us-east-1]
    model_preferences: ["redwood-pico-1b-quant", "redwood-small-3b"]
- Tool calling: we’ll include a sample function schema and the expected tool response stub; the app demonstrates parsing the tool output and re-invoking the model with the tool result as context for structured extraction.
- Embedding shape: we’ll include example using 1536-dim embeddings (recommended for the small reranker) and a script to convert to FAISS index locally. If Lumina wants higher-dim production models we can swap easily.

I’ll attach a minimal TypeScript sample in the repo and a short README for how to reproduce the end-to-end smoke test.

I’m happy to join the Tue 5/25 kickoff for the hands-on.

— Karthik
Principal Developer Advocate, Redwood Inference

This looks great, thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick answers: 
- API key: yes, we can create a scoped API key for the Lumina test project. I’ve asked our infra team to provision it and will send the key via your secure upload link.
- Sample corpus: attaching an S3 presigned link below for the 1k-doc set (synth/anonymized). Use it for the reranker run.
- Region: prefer us-west-2. No special IP allowlist for the lab; we’ll handle that only for prod.
- Embedding dims: start with 1536 for the eval. If results show headroom we’ll iterate.

Please send the sample bundle and let me know the kickoff time for Tue 5/25. I’m available 09:00–11:30 PT.
